@soltysh completion time is only set when the Job completes successfully. A Failed Job isn't Complete. Setting it when a Job fails breaks compatibility.
@soltysh @janetkuo Hi, sorry to bother but is there any update regarding the appropriate solution?
I suggest to use `terminationTime` (or similar) that could match both cases. Is there any state schema/diagram that can ensure right term usage ?
It would be nice to have this merged by Kubernetes v1.19
@janetkuo what did we decide about this one?
@soltysh any further thoughts on this one? Job has 2 different conditions: `Complete` and `Failed`. It'll be confusing (and breaking) to set `CompletionTime` when a Job fails.

issue_context.title: Kubectl reporting wrong duration for jobs aborted due to exceeding deadline
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

It seems that Jobs that get terminated due to exceeding the active deadline seconds get a wrong duration reported via `kubectl`.

This the `kubectl get jobs` for the affected Jobs:

```
$ kubectl get jobs -l app=material-girl                              
NAME                                          COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1575862380   1/1           4m2s       10d
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1575948780   1/1           3m18s      9d
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576035180   0/1           8d         8d
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576121580   1/1           5m16s      7d10h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576207980   1/1           4m12s      6d10h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576294380   1/1           3m26s      5d10h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576380780   0/1           4d10h      4d10h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180   0/1           3d10h      3d10h <-- This
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576481580   0/1           3d1h       3d1h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576567980   0/1           2d6h       2d6h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576654380   0/1           30h        30h
material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576740780   1/1           3m43s      6h28m
```

There are other Jobs affected by this issue (all of those created via a Cronjob), but let me show one particular example.

Running `kubectl describe` don't give any information about the status of this Job, as it would if it was still running, I think, which is also not expected behavior:

```
Name:                     material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180
Namespace:                default
Selector:                 controller-uid=c7573657-1fb4-11ea-bb06-42010af0026d
Labels:                   app=material-girl
                          bu=information
                          name=material-girl-dashboard-tracking
Annotations:              <none>
Controlled By:            CronJob/material-girl-dashboard-tracking
Parallelism:              1
Completions:              1
Start Time:               Mon, 16 Dec 2019 00:33:08 -0300
Active Deadline Seconds:  900s
Pods Statuses:            0 Running / 0 Succeeded / 1 Failed
Pod Template:
  Labels:  app=material-girl
           bu=information
           controller-uid=c7573657-1fb4-11ea-bb06-42010af0026d
           job-name=material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180
           name=material-girl-dashboard-tracking
  Containers:
   material-girl-dashboard-tracking:
    Image:      redacted
    Port:       <none>
    Host Port:  <none>
    Command:
      redacted
    Limits:
      memory:  128M
    Requests:
      cpu:     200m
      memory:  128M
    Environment Variables from:
      redacted
    Environment:
      redacted
    Mounts:           <none>
  Volumes:            <none>
Events:               <none>
```

This is the YAML manifest for that Job:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2019-12-16T03:33:08Z"
  labels:
    app: material-girl
    bu: information
    name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking
  name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180
  namespace: default
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: CronJob
    name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking
    uid: 00f35158-1041-11ea-948c-42010af002a4
  resourceVersion: "1343281381"
  selfLink: /apis/batch/v1/namespaces/default/jobs/material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180
  uid: c7573657-1fb4-11ea-bb06-42010af0026d
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 900
  backoffLimit: 1
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      controller-uid: c7573657-1fb4-11ea-bb06-42010af0026d
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: material-girl
        bu: information
        controller-uid: c7573657-1fb4-11ea-bb06-42010af0026d
        job-name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking-1576467180
        name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking
      name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - redacted
        env:
        - name: redacted
          value: redacted
        image: redacted
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: material-girl-dashboard-tracking
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 128M
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 128M
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Never
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
status:
  conditions:
  - lastProbeTime: "2019-12-16T03:48:08Z"
    lastTransitionTime: "2019-12-16T03:48:08Z"
    message: Job was active longer than specified deadline
    reason: DeadlineExceeded
    status: "True"
    type: Failed
  failed: 1
  startTime: "2019-12-16T03:33:08Z"
```

Kubectl is reporting the correct duration for Jobs that finished successfully. The only difference is that successful Jobs have a `completionTime` status field that is not being set when the Job aborts due to reaching the active deadline seconds, so this might not be a problem in `kubectl` itself.

This is the status of a Job that succeeded:

```yaml
status:
  completionTime: "2019-12-12T03:38:24Z"
  conditions:
  - lastProbeTime: "2019-12-12T03:38:24Z"
    lastTransitionTime: "2019-12-12T03:38:24Z"
    status: "True"
    type: Complete
  startTime: "2019-12-12T03:33:08Z"
  succeeded: 1
```

**What you expected to happen**:

I expected `kubectl get jobs` to report the correct job duration when job was aborted due to exceeding the active deadline seconds.

I expected `kubectl describe job` to display the status for Jobs aborted due to exceeding the active deadline seconds.

I expected Kubernetes to set the `completionTime` status field for aborted Jobs, maybe?

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

See YAML files above, they should be enough to reproduce the issue.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**: GKE

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  - Server: 1.14.8-gke.12
  - Client: 1.16.3
